joints.name: the Harrier's base: three 4-40 steel screws
the cradle's rail locks: two M3 steel screws in heat-set inserts
the rail on the top plate: four M3 nylon screws

unproven.what: The laminate: iFlight publishes nothing about the Nazgul's carbon, so its stiffness runs 40 to 70 GPa and its strength from 400 MPa, typical woven plate.
unproven.measure: A tap test on a spare arm, clamped as on the frame, with a phone's accelerometer or a microphone: its ring frequency gives the stiffness.

unproven.what: The clamp: where the arm's free length starts depends on how tightly the plates hold it, swept 10% either way here.
unproven.measure: The same tap test on the built frame.

unproven.what: The heat-set inserts' pull-out and the printed cradle and rail: guesses, and the weakest links between the chute's riser and the frame.
unproven.measure: A hang test before P flies: 26 kg (the jolt's bound) from the riser's point on the mounted cradle for a minute, then 39 kg (one and a half times); nothing cracks, creeps or pulls out.

unproven.what: Crashes, and the legs' TPU under a hard landing: no FE model without CalculiX.
unproven.measure: Drop tests of the legs with a dummy weight, from 0.25 m up to 1 m.
